To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

patients who were incompletely treated with percutaneous coronary interventions (PCI) had a 15% increased risk of dying compared with those who were completely treated, even after accounting for differences in preprocedure risk.

incomplete percutaneous coronary interventions (PCI) are associated with a higher risk of death, and that this increased mortality is greatest in those with total occlusion of the left main coronary artery or ≥2 incompletely treated lesions.
incomplete revascularization is common after stenting for multivessel coronary disease and is associated with an increase in long-term mortality and the need for repeat procedures.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the impact of incomplete percutaneous coronary revascularization (PCI) on subsequent mortality and subsequent re-intervention.
the long-term outcomes of patients undergoing percutaneous coronary interventions.
the impact of completeness of percutaneous coronary revascularization with stents on long-term survival.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
incomplete revascularization is a marker of increased risk for death and that the risk increases as the degree of incomplete revascularizations increases.
the incomplete revascularization with percutaneous coronary interventions is associated with adverse outcomes.

the completeness of revascularisation by percutaneous intervention is an independent predictor of long-term mortality and that patients with total occlusion or two or more IR vessels are at the highest risk.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the completeness of revascularisation is an important predictor of long-term mortality in the stent era.
the impact of IR is greater than previously recognized, especially in patients with total occlusion and ≥2 IR vessels.
patients who are incompletely revascularised with a stent have an increased risk for death.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the completeness of revascularizaton with stenting is an important factor in the long term outcomes of patients undergoing stenting for multi-vessel disease.
incomplete revascularization with stenting is an adverse prognostic factor for long-term survival.
patients who are incompletely revascularization with stents have worse outcomes than patients who are completely revascularized.
